body:
Second sweep, different axis: degenerate and boundary inputs on the happy path rather than wrong-type arguments. Thirty-odd probes across partition counts, single-feature and single-condition geometries, duplicate and mismatched names, degenerate spatial specs, and non-finite data.

THE VALIDATION IS GENUINELY GOOD AND I WANT THAT ON THE RECORD FIRST. Everything below refused correctly, with messages that name the requirement:

  one partition            At least two distinct, non-missing partitions are required.
  duplicate effect names   Effect coordinates must have unique nonempty names.
  unknown contrast name    Named contrast weights must identify every effect exactly once.
  wrong contrast length    A contrast must contain one finite numeric weight per effect.
  radius 0 or negative     radius must be one positive finite number.
  wrong-length labels      Region labels must have one entry per domain feature.
  NA or Inf in responses   Matrix response sources must be finite and nonempty.
  rdm on 1 condition       An RDM requires at least two experimental effects.

Single-feature and single-condition geometries both build correctly. That is a better boundary story than most packages have.

ONE REAL BUG, bd-01KZYMN0A7F5C65TJN16T2WR91. regions() accepts NA labels, silently drops those features from every region, and silently rescales the regions that lose members:

  r1,r1,r2,r2   ->  feature mass 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5   dropped 0
  r1,r1,NA,r2   ->  feature mass 0.5, 0.5, 0,   1     dropped 1
  r1,NA,NA,r2   ->  feature mass 1,   0,   0,   1     dropped 2

Region r2 stops being the mean of features 3 and 4 and becomes feature 4 alone. Different estimand, no warning, structurally valid frame. Atlas label vectors routinely carry NA for unlabelled voxels, so this is the normal shape of the data the argument exists to accept.

The policy itself - NA means belongs to no region - is defensible and probably right. What is not defensible is that it is SILENT, in a package that refuses non-finite response DATA outright with 'Matrix response sources must be finite and nonempty'. Non-finite data is rejected; non-finite labels are silently honoured. Those two policies disagree.

ONE CONSISTENCY QUESTION, bd-01KZYMPD8H2A2C7HZ0V2X6DGCB. contrast() honours names when present and falls back to position when absent, so unnamed weights in the wrong order silently compute a different contrast. That is ordinary R and I am not proposing to remove it. But it is precisely the identity-from-position inference the rest of this package refuses, and the protection is opt-in: the user who names their weights is checked, the user who does not is not. Cheapest fix is to have print() show the resolved weights with names attached.

METHOD NOTE, since this is now two productive sweeps. Both bugs today and both of these came from CALLING things, never from reading. Four reviewers reading documentation found none of them. Anyone continuing this work should exercise the surface rather than audit it.
